fields.sections.0.h: Simultaneous discoveries across three fields and academic community collaboration approach
fields.sections.2.h: Complete resolution of the local smoothing conjecture in harmonic analysis
fields.sections.3.h: Computational complexity implications of refuting the exponential time hypothesis
fields.sections.4.h: Rigorous existence proofs for quantum chromodynamics and the standard model
fields.sections.5.h: Advantages and disadvantages of the collaboration approach and feedback openness
fields.sections.6.h: Anticipated transition of quantum field theory toward mathematical rigor
fields.sections.0.ko: OpenAI announced new mathematical discoveries in harmonic analysis, computational complexity theory, and quantum field theory. This disclosure approach treats AI outputs as 'raw research data' and invites external expert groups as 'shepherds (guides)' to convert them into substantive academic understanding. The disclosure strategy was differentiated by field: mathematics was fully disclosed to respect researchers' autonomous interpretation, computer science was explained alongside a collaboration group with the original also disclosed, and physics left the disclosure timeline to the collaboration group's judgment.
fields.sections.1.ko: In conducting this collaboration, OpenAI presented four principles: transparency, academic credit, acknowledgment, and independence. Transparency means disclosing the existence of collaboration and allowing participants to avoid non-disclosure agreements; academic credit means OpenAI does not claim authorship of its discoveries. The acknowledgment and independence principles specify that the collaboration group receives full credit for their explanations and writings, participates voluntarily and without compensation, and does not represent OpenAI.
fields.sections.2.ko: The mathematical discovery is a complete proof of the local smoothing conjecture presented in 1991. This conjecture states that wave concentration phenomena, however extreme, must persist only briefly—a fundamental pattern appearing across mathematics in the difference between worst-case and average scenarios. Guth, Wang, and Zhang proved it in two dimensions in 2019, and Wang and Zahl proved the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions in 2025; however, OpenAI's model derived proofs across all dimensions, simultaneously resolving both the Kakeya conjecture and the Stein restriction conjecture. OpenAI obtained this result on October 18, formalized it in Lean the following day, and disclosed it.
fields.sections.3.ko: The subject of computer science collaboration is a proof refuting the exponential time hypothesis (ETH). Regarded over the past 30 years as a foundational conjecture in each field and serving as the basis for hundreds of papers in graph theory, bioinformatics, databases, and computational geometry, this hypothesis was refuted by OpenAI's model and verified in Lean. This result is deeply connected to the P versus NP problem, and if confirmed, will fundamentally reassess the scope for algorithmic acceleration. The collaboration group was composed of top complexity theorists including Impagliazzo and Paturi from UC San Diego and Williams from MIT. OpenAI committed to disclosing all raw data and funding academic conferences to discuss the impact on this field.
fields.sections.4.ko: The physics collaboration addresses rigorous proof of the existence of interacting quantum field theory with gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions. This includes completing the unification of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) and the standard model, and resolves pure Yang-Mills theory, one of the Millennium Prize Problems. The collaboration group was composed of Nobel laureate David Gross, Mikhail Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov. OpenAI obtained the Yang-Mills existence proof on September 9 and the QCD proof on September 18, but began collaboration on October 16 after completing formalization.
fields.sections.5.ko: OpenAI clarifies that the three collaboration approaches carry different advantages and disadvantages. The advantage is that field experts can interpret the significance of results and place them in broader academic context; the disadvantage is that initial shepherd selection may constrain subsequent participant composition and create information asymmetry. The authors actively welcome community feedback to continuously improve this process and are exploring ways to expand participation.
fields.sections.6.ko: OpenAI evaluates this achievement as a first step in quantum field theory—the core framework of modern theoretical physics—transitioning into a mathematically rigorous field. To support this, it contributed $5 million to the Simons Foundation, which will fund workshops, academic conferences, and special programs for researchers to understand and advance AI-generated results. OpenAI expressed its commitment to promoting academically-led progress through such resource support.
fields.caveat: The discoveries in the source are claimed by OpenAI to have been obtained through its AI models and have not yet undergone complete independent verification by the academic community, so they should be subject to academic review before being regarded as scientifically confirmed.
